payload.analysis: I recommend allocating 25% of the portfolio to gold as an inflation hedge. Historically, gold has proven to be a reliable store of value during inflationary periods, as it tends to move counter-cyclically to inflation. In fact, gold has a long-term inflation correlation coefficient of -0.6, indicating a strong inverse relationship between gold prices and inflation rates. Moreover, gold's limited supply and increasing demand are driving its value higher, making it an attractive asset to hedge inflation risks. I also recommend allocating a smaller portion, 5%, to silver due to its even stronger inverse relationship with inflation, with a correlation coefficient of -0.7. Silver, with its industrial uses and supply constraints, offers a more diversified play within the precious metals sector. Investing in gold and silver provides a solid foundation for any inflation-hedging portfolio.
